title: Perturbation Training for Reactive Balance in People With Parkinson's Disease
official: Perturbation Training for Improving Reactive Stepping Responses to Prevent Falls in Parkinson's Disease (ReSteP) - A Randomized Controlled Trial
summary: The objective of this randomized controlled trial is to evaluate the efficacy and feasibility of perturbation-based balance training (PBT) for improving reactive balance and preventing falls in people with Parkinson's Disease (PwPD). Participants will be randomly allocated to either an intervention group, undergoing treadmill-based PBT, or an active control group, performing conventional treadmill training without additional perturbations (CTT). Both groups will receive 12 training sessions within 4 to 6 weeks and will undergo assessments at baseline, post-intervention and 6-month follow-up. The primary outcome is reactive balance in response to perturbations during treadmill walking. Key secondary outcome is reactive balance in response to perturbations during standing. Further secondary outcomes include real-life falls, feasibility and acceptability of the intervention, balance and gait performance, concerns about falling and balance confidence, and disease-related motor symptoms.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Parkinson's Disease diagnosed (MDS diagnostic criteria)
* Stage of the Parkinson's Disease: Hoehn \& Yahr ≤ 3
* Increased fall risk: ≥1 fall in the previous 12 months or ≥ 12 seconds in the Timed Up and Go Test
* Stable medication for at least 4 weeks
* Age: 40 to 85 years

Exclusion Criteria:

* Unable to provide informed consent
* Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score ≤ 17 and significant functional impairment resulting from cognitive impairment (e.g., inability to manage medications or finances independently)
* Atypical Parkinsonism
* Comorbidities: Neurological, cardiovascular, pulmonary, orthopedic or psychiatric contraindications for the planned treadmill interventions
* Deep brain stimulation
* Concurrent enrollment in other interventional clinical trials involving pharmacological treatment and/or structured physical training programs
* Prior experience with structured perturbation training programs systematically involving gait perturbations in the past 2 years
* Inability to walk on the treadmill without assistance for at least 2 minutes at 70% of habitual overground gait speed (assessed during screening)
* Body weight \> 135 kg (exceeds the treadmill manufacturer's specified weight limit)
